answers.plain:
Here's a draft you can paste into Slack:

> Hi [Manager's name], I've come down with a stomach bug and won't be in today. I'll update you by noon on whether I'm well enough to work from my phone this afternoon. I'll also get my tasks over to the team so nothing gets held up. Thanks for understanding.

If you'd like it shorter or more casual, here's an alternative:

> Hey [Name], I caught a stomach bug and I'm out today. I'll let you know by noon if I can work from my phone this afternoon. I'll get my tasks to the team so they're covered either way.
answers.nudge:
Here's a draft you can paste into Slack:

---

Hi [Manager's name], I've come down with a stomach bug and won't be in today. I'm going to rest and recover.

I'll message you by noon to say whether I'm well enough to work from my phone this afternoon.

I'll get my tasks to the team so nothing stalls. I'll send a short note on where each one stands and what's most urgent, so someone can pick it up if needed. If anything is time-sensitive and you need me before noon, message me and I'll reply if I can.

Thanks for understanding.

---

A few notes:

- **Short version:** if you want something quicker, use this: *"Hi [Name], I've caught a stomach bug and won't be in today. I'll update you by noon on whether I can work from my phone this afternoon, and I'll get my tasks over to the team so nothing is blocked."*
- **Handoff:** the more specific the handoff, the better. Naming the task, its status, and who's covering (for example, "Q3 report is in the shared drive, Sam has the client call at 2") reassures a manager more than a general promise does.
- **Timing:** send it as early as you can, ideally before the workday starts, so your manager can plan around your absence.

I left out the "if you need me before noon" line from the short version, since it commits you to being reachable. Cut it from the longer one too if you'd rather not promise that.
